cohort: 78,283 pregnancies with estimated conception before April 30, 2020, and pregnancy end after March 11, 2020, in the United States
finding: Prenatal SARS-CoV-2 infection was not associated with miscarriage, antepartum hemorrhage, or stillbirth, but it was associated with a 2-3 fold higher risk of induced abortion, cesarean delivery, clinician-initiated preterm birth, spontaneous preterm birth, and fetal growth restriction.
mod_finding: SARS-CoV-2 infection during pregnancy was associated with a 2-3 fold increased risk of cesarean delivery.
